complexity.correctness_reason: Arrival times are compared as floats, so once the value cap is lifted two distinct rational times (e.g. 1 and 1 + 10^-18 with target ~ 2*10^18) can round to the same double and two separate fleets get merged into one; within NeetCode's caps (values <= 10^6) the double comparison is provably exact enough.
complexity.notes: Remove the debug print and the now-unused math import before submitting. `List` is never imported from typing; harmless on CPython 3.14 since PEP 649 defers annotation evaluation, but adding the import would be tidier. Comparing (target-p1)*s2 >= (target-p2)*s1 in integers would avoid float precision entirely. Given the benchmark's scaling (target ~ 2n), an O(n) alternative exists via ||indexing cars by position in an array of size target and scanning from the finish line||, though that degrades to O(n + target) on the generalized problem.
complexity.summary: Sorts cars by position, then walks from the car nearest the target outward, comparing float arrival times: a car that would arrive no later than the current lead joins its fleet, otherwise it starts a new fleet and becomes the lead.
